title: Advisory-lock helper (optional): session or transaction level per the Postgres explicit-locking reference, elicited default off
description: The facade exposes an optional advisory-lock helper that wraps pg_advisory_lock and pg_advisory_unlock for session-level locks, and pg_advisory_xact_lock for transaction-level locks. The helper takes an integer lock key, acquires the lock, runs a callback, and releases the lock via the paired unlock verb on the session-level shape (transaction-level locks release automatically at COMMIT or ROLLBACK per https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html). Whether the helper ships in the applied surface is elicited (advisoryLockHelper: off, session, or transaction); default off per the ratified Q1 answer on the round-5 spec section 10. The elicited value is recorded on the applied sidecar so a later validation pass can flag surfaces that never activated the option.
rationale: Cross-process coordination on a shared Postgres (a migration coordinator, a lock-per-tenant workflow, a one-writer-per-partition pattern) is served cleanly by advisory locks; the alternative (a bespoke locks table) reinvents what the engine already gives. Shipping the helper in v1.0.0 pins the semantics before a project depends on a workaround; defaulting off keeps the applied surface small for projects that do not need it. The session-vs-transaction distinction is load-bearing: session-level locks survive rolled-back transactions per the explicit-locking reference, and pinning the choice in the ADR is what avoids the reader-side confusion.
